This file provides guidance to Coding Agent when working with code in this repository.

## What is PegaInfer

Pure Rust + CUDA LLM inference engine. No PyTorch, no frameworks. OpenAI-compatible `/v1/completions` API.

**Supported models:**

Every model line is behind a cargo feature; only `qwen3` is a default feature, so the stock build is pure Rust + CUDA with no Python.

| Model | Crate | Feature flag | Architecture |
|-------|-------|-------------|-------------|
| Qwen3-4B / 8B | `pegainfer-qwen3` | `qwen3` (default) | Full attention, TP support |
| Qwen3.5-4B / 9B / 27B · Qwen3.8-27B | `pegainfer-qwen35` | `--features qwen35` (needs build-time Python + Triton) | Hybrid Gated DeltaNet + full attention. Qwen3.8 shares the line: same `model_type`, same text geometry — see `docs/models/qwen35/support-qwen38.md` |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite | `pegainfer-deepseek-v2-lite` | `--features deepseek-v2-lite` | MoE + EP, 2-GPU |
| Gemma 4 | `pegainfer-gemma4` | `--features gemma4` | Sliding-window + global full attention, dense sizes at TP2 (one rank per device), batched decode, opt-in chunked prefill (single rank only) |
| Kimi-K2 | `pegainfer-kimi-k2` | `--features kimi-k2` | MLA + MoE + Marlin INT4, 8-GPU EP |
| GLM5.2 | `pegainfer-glm52` | `--features glm52` | MLA + MoE + FP8, 8-GPU EP (bring-up) |
| Kimi-K3 | `pegainfer-k3` | `--features k3` | Hybrid KDA + MLA, latent MoE + MXFP4, EP (bring-up — single-rank decode wired) |

## Build & Run

**Always use `--release`** — debug builds are extremely slow for GPU/CUDA and will timeout.

When developing with Docker, use `docker/Dockerfile.dev` and `docker/dev.sh` as described in `docker/README.md`.

```bash
# Qwen3 (default feature, no Python anywhere in the build)
cargo run --release -- --model-path models/Qwen3-4B

# Feature-gated models
cargo run --release --features qwen35 -- --model-path models/Qwen3.5-4B
cargo run --release --features kimi-k2 -- --model-path models/Kimi-K2
cargo run --release --features deepseek-v2-lite -- --model-path models/DeepSeek-V2-Lite
cargo run --release --features glm52 -- --model-path models/GLM5.2
```

**Key env vars:**
- `PEGAINFER_CUDA_SM` — GPU SM target override when `nvidia-smi` unavailable (e.g. `120` or `120,80`)
- `PEGAINFER_TRITON_PYTHON` — Python with Triton for `qwen35` build-time AOT kernel generation (falls back to `.venv/bin/python`, then `python3`, then `python`)
- `PEGAINFER_TILELANG_PYTHON` — Python with TileLang for the `glm52` sparse-MLA build-time AOT (sm_90a targets only)
- `PEGAINFER_NCCL_ROOT` — NCCL root (>= 2.30.4) for DeepEP shim (`moe` feature)
- `PEGAINFER_FLASHINFER_INCLUDE` — FlashInfer include dir override
- `PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH` — override test model path (default: `models/Qwen3-4B`)
- `PEGAINFER_BUILD_TIMING=1` — print per-phase build timings (nvcc, Triton AOT, etc.)
- `PEGAINFER_NVCC_JOBS` — override parallel nvcc job count
- `PEGAINFER_GEMM_LT_CACHE` — opt-in cross-process cublasLt algo store: `<file>` carries the winners `gemm_lt_tune` timed in an earlier boot instead of re-timing them (Qwen3-4B on one sm_89 card: warm ready ~1965 → ~1312 ms, paired 5/5). Append-only text, created if absent, safe to share between processes and machines and safe to delete; each record carries GPU, CUDA runtime/driver/cublasLt version, shape and workspace cap, so anything that does not match is a miss and re-tunes (a driver update that keeps the same CUDA level is not distinguished — delete the file to force a re-tune). Unset = tune on every boot; Qwen3's `--batch-invariant` pins the heuristic instead and never reads it
- `PEGAINFER_GLOBAL_ATTN` — gemma4 global-attention kernel and pool format: unset/`off` = the incumbent kernel on the split K|V pool (byte-identical serving); `tilelang` = the generated kernel on the same pool; `tilelang640` = the generated kernel on a folded pool whose rows hold K only where the rotation touches it and fold K's norm weight into the query, 640 columns per token per head instead of 1024. Both generated states also read the sliding family's prompt rows through a generated windowed prefill and its pure-decode rows through a generated windowed split-KV kernel, project Q|K|V and gate|up with one GEMM each where the split state issues one per projection (the fused shape may round differently), need a build that carries the kernels, and report the global pool's bytes at start-up
- `PEGAINFER_KV_FP8` — gemma4 opt-in fp8 KV: `local` stores the sliding family's K/V as e4m3 at scale 1.0 (lossy; halves the local pool; refuses an enabled prefix cache; unset = byte-identical serving)
- `PEGAINFER_PREFIX_CACHE` — gemma4 opt-in conversation prefix cache: `K` entries of captured prompt state resume multi-turn prompts (pre-allocated page budget; unset = off, byte-identical serving)
- `PEGAINFER_ADMIT_COALESCE_MS` — gemma4 opt-in admission coalesce door: `N` ms in `1..=2000` (`off`/`0`/unset = admit on sight), holds arrivals that would invade a live decode batch so a window's arrivals land as one admission burst; refuses the async prefill lane; merging into one mixed step needs the chunked walk or a sub-budget prompt
- `PEGAINFER_ASYNC_PREFILL` — gemma4 opt-in overlap lane: `green:NN` prefills live-batch admissions on an SM-capped stream to protect decode tails (`shared` for comparison; unset = off; bad values refuse to start)
- `PEGAINFER_MIX_CHUNK_TOKENS` — gemma4 opt-in chunked walk: a mixed admission computes at most `N` prompt rows per step (`64 <= N <` the serving ceiling; unset = whole-prompt steps; bad values refuse to start)
- `PEGAINFER_MIX_GATHER_ROWS` / `PEGAINFER_MIX_MAX_PROMPTS` — gemma4 admission gather: how many prompt rows and how many prompts one mixed step may absorb (`1..=` the serving ceiling and `1..=` the decode slots; defaults gather only short bursts). Raising them lets a burst ride one step, which trades the median time to first token for the p99 tail and the wide-batch decode step; bad values refuse to start
- `PEGAINFER_MAX_CONTEXT` — gemma4 serving ceiling raise (default 8192, up to the checkpoint's 262144; a raise past the default needs `PEGAINFER_MIX_CHUNK_TOKENS` and refuses the async lane)
- `PEGAINFER_DECODE_SLOTS` — gemma4 decode slots (1..16, default 16): global KV budget = slots x ceiling, trade concurrency for context
- `GLM52_DECODE_SLOTS` / `GLM52_MTP_DRAFTS` — glm52 runtime profile: decode slots per rank (default 8, ceiling 32) and MTP draft span (default 5); `slots x (1+drafts)` must fit the 96-row step (validated at launch; MTP only). Throughput ceiling profile: `32` / `2`.
- `PEGAINFER_K3_CP` — k3 opt-in context-parallel prefill lane: CP width, must equal the process's local rank count (on a fleet each process runs its own gang; remote ranks pad). Mutually exclusive with the dspark draft lane.
- `PEGAINFER_K3_CP_MIN` — k3 CP admission floor in prompt tokens (default 2048; measured crossover ~1k). Prompts below it, or too long for one chunk step per rank (M0), prefill locally.

## Tests

```bash
# Unit tests (~9s)
cargo test --release --workspace --lib

# Lines gated on their own kernel feature need it named to run their unit tests.
# The K3 command also names the kernels crate, whose K3 tests ride the same
# feature:
cargo test --release -p pegainfer-k3 -p pegainfer-kernels --features k3 --lib
cargo test --release -p pegainfer-glm52 --features glm52 --lib

# Accuracy and integration tests — require GPU + model weights
cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen3 --test hf_golden_gate
PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH=models/Qwen3.5-4B cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen35 --features qwen35 --test hf_golden_gate
PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH=models/Qwen3.5-4B cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen35 --features qwen35 --test e2e_scheduler

# Single test (filter by name)
cargo test --release --workspace --lib prefix_cache -- --nocapture
```

Qwen accuracy gates compare logits against stored HF golden fixtures. Qwen3.5 exact-text JSON baselines are retired; keep `e2e_scheduler` for scheduler liveness and request-flow coverage.

## Architecture

```
HTTP Request → vLLM frontend → EngineHandle → per-model scheduler/executor → TokenEvent
                                               │
              ┌──────────┬─────────────┬───────┼───────────┬──────────┐
              │          │             │       │           │          │
        pegainfer-  pegainfer-   pegainfer-  pegainfer-  pegainfer-  ...
        qwen3       qwen35       dsv2-lite   kimi-k2     glm52
      (full attn) (linear+full) (MoE+EP)   (MLA+MoE)  (MLA+MoE+FP8)
              │          │             │       │           │          │
              └──────────┴─────────────┴───────┼───────────┴──────────┘
                                               │
                          pegainfer-core runtime + pegainfer-kernels
                                               │
                               ┌───────────────┼───────────────┐
                               │               │               │
                       CUDA / cuBLAS    Triton AOT      FlashInfer
                                                    (sampling, attention,
                                                     norm, MLA decode)

Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## What is PegaInfer

Pure Rust + CUDA LLM inference engine. No PyTorch, no frameworks. OpenAI-compatible `/v1/completions` API.

**Supported models:**

Every model line is behind a cargo feature; only `qwen3` is a default feature, so the stock build is pure Rust + CUDA with no Python.

| Model | Crate | Feature flag | Architecture |
|-------|-------|-------------|-------------|
| Qwen3-4B / 8B | `pegainfer-qwen3` | `qwen3` (default) | Full attention, TP support |
| Qwen3.5-4B / 9B / 27B · Qwen3.8-27B | `pegainfer-qwen35` | `--features qwen35` (needs build-time Python + Triton) | Hybrid Gated DeltaNet + full attention. Qwen3.8 shares the line: same `model_type`, same text geometry — see `docs/models/qwen35/support-qwen38.md` |

| Gemma 4 | `pegainfer-gemma4` | `--features gemma4` | Sliding-window + global full attention, dense sizes at TP2 (one rank per device), batched decode, opt-in chunked prefill (single rank only) |

| GLM5.2 | `pegainfer-glm52` | `--features glm52` | MLA + MoE + FP8, 8-GPU EP (bring-up) |
| Kimi-K3 | `pegainfer-k3` | `--features k3` | Hybrid KDA + MLA, latent MoE + MXFP4, EP (bring-up — single-rank decode wired) |

## Build & Run

cargo run --release -- --model-path models/Qwen3-4B

# Feature-gated models
cargo run --release --features qwen35 -- --model-path models/Qwen3.5-4B
cargo run --release --features kimi-k2 -- --model-path models/Kimi-K2
cargo run --release --features deepseek-v2-lite -- --model-path models/DeepSeek-V2-Lite
cargo run --release --features glm52 -- --model-path models/GLM5.2

**Key env vars:**
- `PEGAINFER_CUDA_SM` — GPU SM target override when `nvidia-smi` unavailable (e.g. `120` or `120,80`)
- `PEGAINFER_TRITON_PYTHON` — Python with Triton for `qwen35` build-time AOT kernel generation (falls back to `.venv/bin/python`, then `python3`, then `python`)
- `PEGAINFER_TILELANG_PYTHON` — Python with TileLang for the `glm52` sparse-MLA build-time AOT (sm_90a targets only)
- `PEGAINFER_NCCL_ROOT` — NCCL root (>= 2.30.4) for DeepEP shim (`moe` feature)
- `PEGAINFER_FLASHINFER_INCLUDE` — FlashInfer include dir override
- `PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH` — override test model path (default: `models/Qwen3-4B`)
- `PEGAINFER_BUILD_TIMING=1` — print per-phase build timings (nvcc, Triton AOT, etc.)
- `PEGAINFER_NVCC_JOBS` — override parallel nvcc job count
- `PEGAINFER_GEMM_LT_CACHE` — opt-in cross-process cublasLt algo store: `<file>` carries the winners `gemm_lt_tune` timed in an earlier boot instead of re-timing them (Qwen3-4B on one sm_89 card: warm ready ~1965 → ~1312 ms, paired 5/5). Append-only text, created if absent, safe to share between processes and machines and safe to delete; each record carries GPU, CUDA runtime/driver/cublasLt version, shape and workspace cap, so anything that does not match is a miss and re-tunes (a driver update that keeps the same CUDA level is not distinguished — delete the file to force a re-tune). Unset = tune on every boot; Qwen3's `--batch-invariant` pins the heuristic instead and never reads it
- `PEGAINFER_GLOBAL_ATTN` — gemma4 global-attention kernel and pool format: unset/`off` = the incumbent kernel on the split K|V pool (byte-identical serving); `tilelang` = the generated kernel on the same pool; `tilelang640` = the generated kernel on a folded pool whose rows hold K only where the rotation touches it and fold K's norm weight into the query, 640 columns per token per head instead of 1024. - `PEGAINFER_PREFIX_CACHE` — gemma4 opt-in conversation prefix cache: `K` entries of captured prompt state resume multi-turn prompts (pre-allocated page budget; unset = off, byte-identical serving)
- `PEGAINFER_ADMIT_COALESCE_MS` — gemma4 opt-in admission coalesce door: `N` ms in `1..=2000` (`off`/`0`/unset = admit on sight), holds arrivals that would invade a live decode batch so a window's arrivals land as one admission burst; refuses the async prefill lane; merging into one mixed step needs the chunked walk or a sub-budget prompt

- `PEGAINFER_MIX_CHUNK_TOKENS` — gemma4 opt-in chunked walk: a mixed admission computes at most `N` prompt rows per step (`64 <= N <` the serving ceiling; unset = whole-prompt steps; bad values refuse to start)

## Architecture

```
HTTP Request → vLLM frontend → EngineHandle → per-model scheduler/executor → TokenEvent
                                               │
              ┌──────────┬─────────────┬───────┼───────────┬──────────┐
              │          │             │       │           │          │
        pegainfer-  pegainfer-   pegainfer-  pegainfer-  pegainfer-  ...
        qwen3       qwen35       dsv2-lite   kimi-k2     glm52

              │          │             │       │           │          │
              └──────────┴─────────────┴───────┼───────────┴──────────┘
                                               │
                          pegainfer-core runtime + pegainfer-kernels
                                               │
                               ┌───────────────┼───────────────┐
                               │               │               │
                       CUDA / cuBLAS    Triton AOT      FlashInfer
                                                    (sampling, attention,
                                                     norm, MLA decode)
```

**Key abstractions:**

- **`pegainfer-frontend`** — the serving frontend: the engine request/event contract (`pegainfer_frontend::engine` — `EngineHandle`, `GenerateRequest`, `TokenEvent`) plus the protocol stacks on top of it (`vllm` module today, `dynamo` planned) and the `ModelLine` dispatch trait. Model crates implement against the contract; the server binary does pure dispatch.
- **Per-model crates** — each model owns config, weights, prefill/decode execution, scheduler, tests, and benches.
- **`pegainfer-core::ops`** — shared GPU operator wrappers used by model crates.
- **`pegainfer-kernels`** — tensor/FFI/kernel build owner for CUDA, cuBLAS, FlashInfer, and Triton AOT. Model-specific kernels live in feature-gated submodules (`kimi_k2`, `glm52`).
- **CUDA Graph** — decode path captured inside model executors with pre-allocated buffers to preserve pointer stability.
- **KV state** — model schedulers own request state; shared paged-KV primitives live in `pegainfer-kv-cache`; host/SSD/RDMA offload bridge in `pegainfer-kv-offload`.

**Build system**: the virtual workspace root has no package build script. `pegainfer-kernels/build.rs` owns CUDA/Triton compilation:
1. Compiles `pegainfer-kernels/csrc/*.cu` with nvcc (auto-detects GPU SM targets)
2. Feature-gated codegen: `qwen35` runs Triton AOT via `pegainfer-kernels/tools/triton/gen_triton_aot.py`; `kimi-k2` adds MLA/MoE/Marlin CUDA; `glm52` adds MLA/MoE/FP8 CUDA plus TileLang sparse-MLA codegen on sm_90a

## EP Free-Running Discipline

Canonical doc: `docs/models/glm52/free-running-dp.md` (K3's gang lane follows it). Invariants — violating any of these is a deadlock design:

- **No rank ever stops or waits.** Every engine loop runs unconditionally at full speed; idle ranks step with padding rows. Any quiet wait (condvar, sleep-poll) inside EP coordination is a bug, and the fleet is never asleep, so never design "wake up" or "pump until X" steps.
- **The per-step collective chain is fixed** — no conditional collectives. Skipping work happens inside kernels via zero-load padding entry, never by host negotiation.
- **The launch count is the global clock** (pairing pins all ranks within ±1 launch). Coordination means agreeing ahead of time on *what step N contains*, never "wait until everyone is ready".
- **Padding rows are protocol surface**: their bytes reach peers, so every dummy-row input must be constructively deterministic.

4	
5	学完本讲，你应该能够：
6	
7	1. 追踪一条完整的加载链：磁盘上的 `config.json` → serde 反序列化成 `RawConfig` → `TryFrom` 一次性校验成 `Config35`。

12	## 2. 前置知识
13	
14	- **serde 反序列化**：Rust 最常用的序列化框架。给结构体标上 `#[derive(Deserialize)]`，`serde_json::from_str` 就能把 JSON 文本变成结构体实例。字段类型不匹配、缺了非 `Option` 字段时 serde 直接报错——这是第一道「形状」检查。
15	- **`TryFrom` trait**：Rust 标准库里「可能失败的类型转换」。`impl TryFrom<RawConfig> for Config35` 的意思是：从原始配置转成已验证配置这一步可能失败，失败时返回类型化的 `ConfigError`。它把「校验」收敛到一个编译器可见的边界上。
16	- **fail-closed（失败即关闭）**：宁可拒绝启动，也不带着可疑配置继续跑。与 fail-open（记个警告继续服务）相对。推理引擎里一个错误的维度会导致 CUDA 内核越界或垃圾输出，所以配置加载选择 fail-closed。
17	- **「不可表示非法状态」**：本 crate 反复出现的校验风格——校验只在构造边界做一次，之后下游拿到的类型（这里是 `Config35`）不可能处于非法状态，下游代码因此不需要重复防御。
18	- **词表与 padding 的背景**：检查点的 `vocab_size`（词嵌入矩阵的行数）常常比 tokenizer 实际能解码的 token 数多。多出来的行是训练时对齐硬件的 padding，推理时永远不该被选中。
19	- **GQA / 线性注意力头**：全注意力层里 `num_attention_heads` 个 Q 头共享 `num_key_value_heads` 个 KV 头（GQA，要求前者是后者的整数倍）；线性注意力层有自己的 `linear_num_key_heads` / `linear_num_value_heads`，同样要求整除。这些是第 3 单元的主角，本讲只需要知道「整除性是配置期就要保证的不变量」。

36	### 4.1 serde 反序列化：磁盘上的 config.json 如何变成 RawConfig
37	
38	#### 4.1.1 概念说明
39	
40	Qwen3.5 的 `config.json` 是嵌套结构：顶层放全局字段和一个 `text_config` 块，块内才是文本模型的几何参数。本 crate 的策略是**忠实镜像磁盘结构**：定义与 JSON 一一对应的 `RawConfig` / `TextConfig` / `RopeParameters` 三个「原始」结构体，serde 只负责把 JSON 变成它们，**不做任何跨字段判断**。
41	
42	这样切分带来一个清晰的两级错误通道：
43	
44	- serde 负责**形状**：字段类型对不对、必填字段在不在。出错时走 `anyhow`（`from_file` 里 `serde_json::from_str(&content)?` 的 `?`）。
45	- `ConfigError` 负责**语义**：跨字段规则、内核兼容规则。这是 4.2 的内容。
46	
47	一个容易忽略的细节：`tie_word_embeddings` 和 `max_position_embeddings` 在 `RawConfig` 的顶层和 `TextConfig` 里都是 `Option`——因为 HF 检查点这两个字段的位置不统一，可能在外层也可能在内层，「两处都没有」才是错误，而那要等到校验阶段用类型化变体报告，所以 serde 不能把它们定成必填。
48	
49	#### 4.1.2 核心流程
50	
51	```
52	config.json（磁盘 JSON 文本）
53	   │  fs::read_to_string
54	   ▼
55	serde_json::from_str → RawConfig { text_config, max_position_embeddings?, tie_word_embeddings? }
56	   │                     TextConfig { hidden_size, ..., layer_types: Vec<String>, ... }
57	   │  TryFrom<RawConfig> for Config35（4.2）
58	   ▼
59	Config35（已验证：layer_types 已变成 Vec<LayerType>，全部不变量成立）
60	```

94	**练习 1**：如果把 `TextConfig.hidden_size` 的类型从 `usize` 改成 `bool`，错误是在 serde 阶段还是 `TryFrom` 阶段报出来？

96	**答案**：serde 阶段。`serde_json::from_str` 发现 JSON 里是数字、目标类型是 `bool`，直接反序列化失败，走 `anyhow` 通道，根本到不了 `TryFrom`。
97	
98	**练习 2**：为什么 `tie_word_embeddings` 在两个结构体里都是 `Option<bool>` 而不是 `bool` + `#[serde(default)]`？
99	
100	**答案**：`#[serde(default)]` 会把「缺失」和「false」混为一谈。而这里的语义是「外层和内层至少出现一处才算有效」——区分「缺失」与「取值」正是后续 `t.tie_word_embeddings.or(root_tie_word_embeddings)` 回退逻辑的前提，缺失必须能被识别出来并转成 `MissingTieWordEmbeddings` 类型化错误。
101	
102	### 4.2 校验边界模式：TryFrom 的一次性全量校验
103	
104	#### 4.2.1 概念说明
105	
106	`Config35` 是下游一切代码（权重加载、内核启动、调度器）共同消费的「已验证配置」。它的模块文档写着：每条跨字段与内核 AOT 规则都在 `try_from` / `from_file` 这**单一边界**上强制执行，下游只能观察到「已知可加载」的模型。这就是「不可表示非法状态」：不是在几十处调用点各自 `assert`，而是让非法配置根本变不成 `Config35`。
107	
108	校验里最有意思的一类是**内核兼容门**。u1-l2 讲过：GDN 的 Triton AOT 内核在构建期就把 head dim 烘焙（bake）进了签名——`GDN_AOT_KEY_HEAD_DIM = 128`、`GDN_AOT_VALUE_HEAD_DIM = 128`；全注意力内核则固定 `head_dim = 256`；因果卷积解码内核支持 `linear_conv_kernel_dim ∈ 1..=4`。这些常量由 `pegainfer-kernels` 拥有，本模块只重导出。文档注释说得直白：「在这里通过的配置，就是内核能跑的配置」——如果不在加载期对拍，一个 `head_dim = 128` 的检查点会在第一次内核启动时才炸出难以理解的 CUDA 错误。
109	
110	错误全部收进 `ConfigError` 枚举而不是自由字符串，价值有二：调用方和测试能对**确切变体**分支（`assert_eq!(err, ConfigError::MissingTieWordEmbeddings)` 这样写测试），加载器能带着精确信息 fail-closed。
111	
112	#### 4.2.2 核心流程
113	
114	`try_from` 的校验按固定顺序执行，**首错即返**：
115	
116	```
117	1. tie_word_embeddings = text_config 值 .or(根值)     缺失 → MissingTieWordEmbeddings
118	2. layer_types: Vec<String> → Vec<LayerType>          未知字符串 → UnknownLayerType
119	3. layer_types.len() == num_hidden_layers             不等 → LayerTypeCountMismatch
120	4. rotary_dim = ⌊head_dim × partial_rotary_factor⌋    为 0 → ZeroRotaryDim
121	5. max_position_embeddings = text_config 值 .or(根值) 缺失 → MissingMaxPositionEmbeddings
122	                                                       为 0 → NonPositiveMaxPositionEmbeddings

208	### 4.3 词表宽度计算：selection_vocab 与 decodable_vocab
209	
210	#### 4.3.1 概念说明
211	
212	`Config35` 里有两个看起来都像「词表大小」的字段，加上检查点自带的 `vocab_size`，一共三个宽度，各司其职：
213	
214	| 字段 | 含义 | 谁用它 |
215	|---|---|---|
216	| `vocab_size` | 检查点词嵌入矩阵的物理行数 | 权重加载、嵌入查表 |
217	| `decodable_vocab` | tokenizer 真正能解码的 token 数（稠密前缀） | argmax 与采样路由的测量基准；超出部分被抑制 |
218	| `selection_vocab` | `decodable_vocab` 向上取整到 128 的倍数、再夹到 `vocab_size` 以内 | logits GEMM 的 M 维、logits 缓冲、采样器 arena |
219	
220	为什么要对齐到 128？`pegainfer-core` 的文档注释给出动机：Qwen3.5-4B 实际可解码 248077 个 id，这是个「坏」宽度——未对齐的 GEMM 维度会把 cublasLt 逼到 align-1 内核，性能大幅受损；取整到 128-token tile 后走快路径。多出来的 `decodable_vocab..selection_vocab` 行是纯 padding，采样前会被压成 `-inf`，永远不可能被选中（pad 抑制的完整链路在 u5-l4 采样一讲）。
221	
222	fail-closed 规则则是反向的边界：如果 tokenizer 比检查点还宽（`effective_vocab > vocab_size`），说明这个检查点根本服务不了这个 tokenizer，直接拒绝加载（`EffectiveVocabExceedsCheckpoint`），而不是悄悄截断输出空间。
223	
224	#### 4.3.2 核心流程
225	
226	三个宽度的推导关系（\(d\) 为可解码宽度，\(v\) 为检查点行数）：
227	
228	\[
229	\text{selection\_vocab} = \min\left(\left\lceil \frac{d}{128} \right\rceil \times 128,\; v\right), \qquad d \le v \text{（否则拒绝）}
230	\]
231	
232	完整时序（都发生在权重加载之前）：
233	
234	```
235	from_file:
236	  RawConfig → Config35          （此时 selection/decodable_vocab 暂置为 vocab_size）
237	  eos_token_ids ← generation_config.json / config.json / text_config 三处按序取 eos_token_id
238	bound_selection_vocab(effective_vocab):     ← 由 weights.rs 在加载权重前调用
239	  effective_vocab = decodable_vocab_width(model_path)   （读 tokenizer 两个文件合并 id 集）
240	  1. effective_vocab > vocab_size ? → EffectiveVocabExceedsCheckpoint，拒绝
241	  2. decodable_vocab = effective_vocab
242	  3. selection_vocab = aligned_logits_rows(effective_vocab, vocab_size)
243	  4. selection_vocab != effective_vocab 时打印一条 info 日志（tile 对齐 padding）
244	```
245	
246	用真实数字手算一遍 Qwen3.5-4B（\(d = 248077\)，\(v = 248320\)，均为仓库文档记载的真实值）：
247	
248	\[
249	\left\lceil \frac{248077}{128} \right\rceil \times 128 = 1939 \times 128 = 248192, \qquad \min(248192,\; 248320) = 248192
250	\]
251	
252	所以 `selection_vocab = 248192`、`decodable_vocab = 248077`，padding 区间是行 248077..248192（115 行）。仓库的性能归因文档里 lm_head 那一行写的正是 248192——理论手算与线上实测对上了。

307	2. **校验面**（4.2）：逐条过 `TryFrom` 的十步流程，记录每步的输入值与结论；手算 `rotary_dim`（夹具：\(256 \times 0.25 = 64\)）；再自选两条规则，写出「如何改夹具触发对应 `ConfigError` 变体」。
308	3. **词表面**（4.3）：手算 `selection_vocab` / `decodable_vocab` 与 padding 区间（夹具无 tokenizer，可自设 \(d\) 值演练三档：\(d < v\) 且对齐后不超、对齐后超被夹、\(d > v\) 被拒）。
309	4. **验证**（可选，需 u1-l2 的构建链）：`cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen35 --features qwen35 --lib config::model` 跑通内嵌测试，确认你改的变体与断言一致。
310	
311	检验标准：报告里的每个数字都能在对应源码行找到出处；三条被拒绝的构造各自只触发**一个**错误变体，且是你预测的那个。
312	
313	## 6. 本讲小结
314	
315	- 配置加载是两级错误通道：serde 管「形状」（字段在不在、类型对不对），`ConfigError` 管「语义」（跨字段与内核不变量）；`Option` 字段的存在让「缺失」能被类型化报告而不是与取值混淆。
316	- `TryFrom<RawConfig> for Config35` 是唯一校验边界：十步有序检查、首错即返；通过之后下游拿到的配置「已知可加载」，无需重复防御。
317	- `layer_types` 在这里完成从字符串到 `LayerType` 的升格，混合架构（full/linear 两种层的排布）自此成为类型里的一等信息。
318	- 内核维度（128/128、256、1..=4）是构建期烘焙的 AOT 常量，配置期对拍让「内核不兼容」在加载时就 fail-closed，而不是首次启动时炸 CUDA 错误。
319	- 三个词表宽度各司其职：`vocab_size`（物理行）→ `decodable_vocab`（稠密可解码前缀，fail-closed 拒绝过宽 tokenizer 与稀疏 id）→ `selection_vocab`（128 对齐、夹紧，喂给 cublasLt 快路径）。
320	- `Config35` 刻意对张量并行无知——TP 几何留给下一讲的 `LocalGeometry`，那是方向性边界的另一半。
321

328	- 对照 pegainfer-core 的 [decodable_vocab.rs](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-core/src/decodable_vocab.rs) 完整注释，理解前端（vLLM）分词器合并契约为什么要被引擎精确镜像；

# u2-l1 config.json 的解析与校验：从 RawConfig 到 Config35

## 1. 本讲目标

学完本讲，你应该能够：

1. 追踪一条完整的加载链：磁盘上的 `config.json` → serde 反序列化成 `RawConfig` → `TryFrom` 一次性校验成 `Config35`。
2. 说出 `layer_types` 字符串数组如何决定每一层是 `FullAttention` 还是 `LinearAttention`，以及这条规则的「混合架构」背景。
3. 解释 `selection_vocab` 与 `decodable_vocab` 两个词表宽度的计算公式、128 对齐的动机，以及「tokenizer 比检查点宽就拒绝加载」的 fail-closed 规则。
4. 逐条列出 `TryFrom` 实现拒绝的非法组合，并对应到 `ConfigError` 的具体变体。

## 2. 前置知识

- **serde 反序列化**：Rust 最常用的序列化框架。给结构体标上 `#[derive(Deserialize)]`，`serde_json::from_str` 就能把 JSON 文本变成结构体实例。字段类型不匹配、缺了非 `Option` 字段时 serde 直接报错——这是第一道「形状」检查。
- **`TryFrom` trait**：Rust 标准库里「可能失败的类型转换」。`impl TryFrom<RawConfig> for Config35` 的意思是：从原始配置转成已验证配置这一步可能失败，失败时返回类型化的 `ConfigError`。它把「校验」收敛到一个编译器可见的边界上。
- **fail-closed（失败即关闭）**：宁可拒绝启动，也不带着可疑配置继续跑。与 fail-open（记个警告继续服务）相对。推理引擎里一个错误的维度会导致 CUDA 内核越界或垃圾输出，所以配置加载选择 fail-closed。
- **「不可表示非法状态」**：本 crate 反复出现的校验风格——校验只在构造边界做一次，之后下游拿到的类型（这里是 `Config35`）不可能处于非法状态，下游代码因此不需要重复防御。
- **词表与 padding 的背景**：检查点的 `vocab_size`（词嵌入矩阵的行数）常常比 tokenizer 实际能解码的 token 数多。多出来的行是训练时对齐硬件的 padding，推理时永远不该被选中。
- **GQA / 线性注意力头**：全注意力层里 `num_attention_heads` 个 Q 头共享 `num_key_value_heads` 个 KV 头（GQA，要求前者是后者的整数倍）；线性注意力层有自己的 `linear_num_key_heads` / `linear_num_value_heads`，同样要求整除。这些是第 3 单元的主角，本讲只需要知道「整除性是配置期就要保证的不变量」。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

| 文件 | 作用 |
|------|------|
| [src/config/mod.rs](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen35/src/config/mod.rs) | config 子模块的目录页：声明 `error` / `model` / `tp` 三个子模块与方向性边界；提供身份探测 `probe_config_json` |
| [src/config/model.rs](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen35/src/config/model.rs) | 本讲主角：`RawConfig` / `TextConfig` 反序列化、`Config35` 定义、`TryFrom` 校验实现、`bound_selection_vocab` 词表宽度计算，以及内嵌单元测试 |
| [src/config/error.rs](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen35/src/config/error.rs) | 类型化错误枚举 `ConfigError`：模型配置、TP 分配两大类共 14 个变体 |
| [src/weights.rs](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen35/src/weights.rs) | 调用方：`from_safetensors*` 里以 `Config35::from_file` 起步、随后调用 `bound_selection_vocab`（下一讲的主角，本讲只看入口几行） |
| pegainfer-core/src/decodable_vocab.rs | 跨模型共享：`decodable_vocab_width` 从 tokenizer 文件算出可解码宽度，`aligned_logits_rows` 做 128 对齐 |
| pegainfer-core/src/eos.rs | 跨模型共享：`eos_token_ids` 按 generation_config → config → text_config 优先级解析 EOS 集合 |

注意 `config/tp.rs` 属于下一讲（u2-l2），本讲刻意不展开——`Config35` 本身对张量并行一无所知，这是模块注释里明写的方向性边界。

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 serde 反序列化：磁盘上的 config.json 如何变成 RawConfig

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

Qwen3.5 的 `config.json` 是嵌套结构：顶层放全局字段和一个 `text_config` 块，块内才是文本模型的几何参数。本 crate 的策略是**忠实镜像磁盘结构**：定义与 JSON 一一对应的 `RawConfig` / `TextConfig` / `RopeParameters` 三个「原始」结构体，serde 只负责把 JSON 变成它们，**不做任何跨字段判断**。

这样切分带来一个清晰的两级错误通道：

- serde 负责**形状**：字段类型对不对、必填字段在不在。出错时走 `anyhow`（`from_file` 里 `serde_json::from_str(&content)?` 的 `?`）。
- `ConfigError` 负责**语义**：跨字段规则、内核兼容规则。这是 4.2 的内容。

一个容易忽略的细节：`tie_word_embeddings` 和 `max_position_embeddings` 在 `RawConfig` 的顶层和 `TextConfig` 里都是 `Option`——因为 HF 检查点这两个字段的位置不统一，可能在外层也可能在内层，「两处都没有」才是错误，而那要等到校验阶段用类型化变体报告，所以 serde 不能把它们定成必填。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

```
config.json（磁盘 JSON 文本）
   │  fs::read_to_string
   ▼
serde_json::from_str → RawConfig { text_config, max_position_embeddings?, tie_word_embeddings? }
   │                     TextConfig { hidden_size, ..., layer_types: Vec<String>, ... }
   │  TryFrom<RawConfig> for Config35（4.2）
   ▼
Config35（已验证：layer_types 已变成 Vec<LayerType>，全部不变量成立）
```

身份探测发生在更早的地方：`probe_config_json` 只回答「这是不是 Qwen3.5」——`model_type == "qwen3_5"`、architectures 含 `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration`、`text_config.model_type == "qwen3_5_text"` 三条全过才算数。模块注释明确说「尺寸与形状校验属于 config 加载器」，即探测与校验是两个职责。这正是 u1-l4 讲过的 probe 两段式，此处不重复。

#### 4.1.3 源码精读

原始结构体完整定义（注意与 JSON 字段名一一对应）：

> [src/config/model.rs:29-58](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen35/src/config/model.rs#L29-L58)：`TextConfig` / `RawConfig` 忠实镜像磁盘 JSON：`layer_types` 此时只是 `Vec<String>`，两个可挪位的字段是 `Option`，serde 阶段不做任何判断。

RoPE 只读两个键：

> [src/config/model.rs:22-27](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen35/src/config/model.rs#L22-L27)：`RopeParameters` 只取 `rope_theta` 和 `partial_rotary_factor`——Qwen3.5 的 RoPE 参数收在 `text_config.rope_parameters` 子对象里，且是部分旋转（partial RoPE）。

文件入口：

> [src/config/mod.rs:24-51](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen35/src/config/mod.rs#L24-L51)：`probe_config_json` 三条身份检查，全过返回 `Ok(())`，任一不过即 `bail!`/`ensure!` 拒绝。

> [src/config/model.rs:119-128](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen35/src/config/model.rs#L119-L128)：`from_file` 是完整加载入口——读文件、serde 反序列化、`try_from` 校验、最后解析 EOS。四步各自可能失败，全部用 `?` 上抛。

一个值得注意的旁证：测试夹具 JSON 里的 `text_config` 带了一个 `"eos_token_id": 0` 键，但 `TextConfig` 根本没有这个字段——serde 默认忽略未知键，EOS 实际由 `pegainfer_core::eos::eos_token_ids` 在 `from_file` 里另行解析（见 4.3.3）。这印证了「原始结构体只镜像自己关心的键」。

#### 4.1.4 代码实践

1. **实践目标**：亲手把一份真实（或夹具）config.json 映射到 `RawConfig` 的字段上。
2. **操作步骤**：
   - 若本地有 Qwen3.5 权重目录，打开 `models/Qwen3.5-4B/config.json`；没有就用 [src/config/model.rs:303-324](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen35/src/config/model.rs#L303-L324) 的 `VALID_RAW` 夹具。
   - 逐个字段抄写到一张两列表：左列 JSON 路径（如 `text_config.linear_key_head_dim`），右列 Rust 结构体字段（如 `TextConfig::linear_key_head_dim`）。
   - 特别标记三个问题字段：`tie_word_embeddings` 和 `max_position_embeddings` 分别出现在 JSON 的哪一层？`layer_types` 是字符串数组还是对象？
3. **需要观察的现象**：HF 发布的检查点里这两个 `Option` 字段的位置确实不统一（有的在外层、有的在 `text_config` 里）；`layer_types` 是纯字符串数组（如 `["linear_attention", "full_attention", ...]`）。
4. **预期结果**：得到一张 20 行左右的映射表，其中没有任何一行需要「计算」——这就是 serde 层的全部职责。待本地验证（取决于你手上有没有真实检查点；夹具路径无需求验证）。

#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：如果把 `TextConfig.hidden_size` 的类型从 `usize` 改成 `bool`，错误是在 serde 阶段还是 `TryFrom` 阶段报出来？

**答案**：serde 阶段。`serde_json::from_str` 发现 JSON 里是数字、目标类型是 `bool`，直接反序列化失败，走 `anyhow` 通道，根本到不了 `TryFrom`。

**练习 2**：为什么 `tie_word_embeddings` 在两个结构体里都是 `Option<bool>` 而不是 `bool` + `#[serde(default)]`？

**答案**：`#[serde(default)]` 会把「缺失」和「false」混为一谈。而这里的语义是「外层和内层至少出现一处才算有效」——区分「缺失」与「取值」正是后续 `t.tie_word_embeddings.or(root_tie_word_embeddings)` 回退逻辑的前提，缺失必须能被识别出来并转成 `MissingTieWordEmbeddings` 类型化错误。

### 4.2 校验边界模式：TryFrom 的一次性全量校验

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

`Config35` 是下游一切代码（权重加载、内核启动、调度器）共同消费的「已验证配置」。它的模块文档写着：每条跨字段与内核 AOT 规则都在 `try_from` / `from_file` 这**单一边界**上强制执行，下游只能观察到「已知可加载」的模型。这就是「不可表示非法状态」：不是在几十处调用点各自 `assert`，而是让非法配置根本变不成 `Config35`。

校验里最有意思的一类是**内核兼容门**。u1-l2 讲过：GDN 的 Triton AOT 内核在构建期就把 head dim 烘焙（bake）进了签名——`GDN_AOT_KEY_HEAD_DIM = 128`、`GDN_AOT_VALUE_HEAD_DIM = 128`；全注意力内核则固定 `head_dim = 256`；因果卷积解码内核支持 `linear_conv_kernel_dim ∈ 1..=4`。这些常量由 `pegainfer-kernels` 拥有，本模块只重导出。文档注释说得直白：「在这里通过的配置，就是内核能跑的配置」——如果不在加载期对拍，一个 `head_dim = 128` 的检查点会在第一次内核启动时才炸出难以理解的 CUDA 错误。

错误全部收进 `ConfigError` 枚举而不是自由字符串，价值有二：调用方和测试能对**确切变体**分支（`assert_eq!(err, ConfigError::MissingTieWordEmbeddings)` 这样写测试），加载器能带着精确信息 fail-closed。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

`try_from` 的校验按固定顺序执行，**首错即返**：

```
1. tie_word_embeddings = text_config 值 .or(根值)     缺失 → MissingTieWordEmbeddings
2. layer_types: Vec<String> → Vec<LayerType>          未知字符串 → UnknownLayerType
3. layer_types.len() == num_hidden_layers             不等 → LayerTypeCountMismatch
4. rotary_dim = ⌊head_dim × partial_rotary_factor⌋    为 0 → ZeroRotaryDim
5. max_position_embeddings = text_config 值 .or(根值) 缺失 → MissingMaxPositionEmbeddings
                                                       为 0 → NonPositiveMaxPositionEmbeddings
6. linear_key/value_head_dim == 128/128（AOT 烘焙值）  不等 → GdnAotHeadDimMismatch
7. head_dim == 256                                    不等 → FullAttnHeadDimMismatch
8. 1 ≤ linear_conv_kernel_dim ≤ 4                     越界 → LinearConvKernelDim
9. linear_num_value_heads % linear_num_key_heads == 0（且后者非 0）
                                                      不整除 → LinearHeadDivisibility
10. num_attention_heads % num_key_value_heads == 0（且后者非 0）
                                                      不整除 → AttentionHeadDivisibility
全部通过 → 构造 Config35（字段原样搬运，selection/decodable_vocab 暂置 vocab_size）
```

其中第 4 步的旋转维度是**截断取整**：

\[
\text{rotary\_dim} = \lfloor \text{head\_dim} \times \text{partial\_rotary\_factor} \rfloor
\]

Rust 的 `as usize` 对浮点做向零截断。夹具里 \(256 \times 0.25 = 64\)，正好整除所以看不出差别；若因子取 0.3，则 \(256 \times 0.3 = 76.8 \to 76\)。部分旋转意味着 Q/K 向量只有前 `rotary_dim` 维参与 RoPE，其余维不旋转——这是 u3-l1 的主题，这里只需要保证算出的值非零。

#### 4.2.3 源码精读

类型与常量：

> [src/config/model.rs:15-20](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen35/src/config/model.rs#L15-L20)：`LayerType` 只有两个变体——「模型级（与 TP 无关）的层排布」这一注释点明它属于 `Config35` 而非分片几何。

> [src/config/model.rs:60-68](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen35/src/config/model.rs#L60-L68)：三个内核常量从 `pegainfer_kernels::ops` 重导出（128/128/4），`FULL_ATTN_HEAD_DIM = 256` 是本模块自己的常量。注释说明 Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 线未来用同一组数字。

校验主体，按上面流程图的顺序逐段对应：

> [src/config/model.rs:197-217](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen35/src/config/model.rs#L197-L217)：字段回退（`or`）与 `LayerType` 字符串匹配（`"full_attention"` / `"linear_attention"` 之外即 `UnknownLayerType`）、长度对账。

> [src/config/model.rs:219-230](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen35/src/config/model.rs#L219-L230)：`rotary_dim` 截断计算与两个「存在性/正性」检查。

### 4.3 词表宽度计算：selection_vocab 与 decodable_vocab

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

`Config35` 里有两个看起来都像「词表大小」的字段，加上检查点自带的 `vocab_size`，一共三个宽度，各司其职：

| 字段 | 含义 | 谁用它 |
|---|---|---|
| `vocab_size` | 检查点词嵌入矩阵的物理行数 | 权重加载、嵌入查表 |
| `decodable_vocab` | tokenizer 真正能解码的 token 数（稠密前缀） | argmax 与采样路由的测量基准；超出部分被抑制 |
| `selection_vocab` | `decodable_vocab` 向上取整到 128 的倍数、再夹到 `vocab_size` 以内 | logits GEMM 的 M 维、logits 缓冲、采样器 arena |

为什么要对齐到 128？`pegainfer-core` 的文档注释给出动机：Qwen3.5-4B 实际可解码 248077 个 id，这是个「坏」宽度——未对齐的 GEMM 维度会把 cublasLt 逼到 align-1 内核，性能大幅受损；取整到 128-token tile 后走快路径。多出来的 `decodable_vocab..selection_vocab` 行是纯 padding，采样前会被压成 `-inf`，永远不可能被选中（pad 抑制的完整链路在 u5-l4 采样一讲）。

fail-closed 规则则是反向的边界：如果 tokenizer 比检查点还宽（`effective_vocab > vocab_size`），说明这个检查点根本服务不了这个 tokenizer，直接拒绝加载（`EffectiveVocabExceedsCheckpoint`），而不是悄悄截断输出空间。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

三个宽度的推导关系（\(d\) 为可解码宽度，\(v\) 为检查点行数）：

\[
\text{selection\_vocab} = \min\left(\left\lceil \frac{d}{128} \right\rceil \times 128,\; v\right), \qquad d \le v \text{（否则拒绝）}
\]

完整时序（都发生在权重加载之前）：

```
from_file:
  RawConfig → Config35          （此时 selection/decodable_vocab 暂置为 vocab_size）
  eos_token_ids ← generation_config.json / config.json / text_config 三处按序取 eos_token_id
bound_selection_vocab(effective_vocab):     ← 由 weights.rs 在加载权重前调用
  effective_vocab = decodable_vocab_width(model_path)   （读 tokenizer 两个文件合并 id 集）
  1. effective_vocab > vocab_size ? → EffectiveVocabExceedsCheckpoint，拒绝
  2. decodable_vocab = effective_vocab
  3. selection_vocab = aligned_logits_rows(effective_vocab, vocab_size)
  4. selection_vocab != effective_vocab 时打印一条 info 日志（tile 对齐 padding）
```

用真实数字手算一遍 Qwen3.5-4B（\(d = 248077\)，\(v = 248320\)，均为仓库文档记载的真实值）：

\[
\left\lceil \frac{248077}{128} \right\rceil \times 128 = 1939 \times 128 = 248192, \qquad \min(248192,\; 248320) = 248192
\]

所以 `selection_vocab = 248192`、`decodable_vocab = 248077`，padding 区间是行 248077..248192（115 行）。仓库的性能归因文档里 lm_head 那一行写的正是 248192——理论手算与线上实测对上了。

## 6. 本讲小结

- 配置加载是两级错误通道：serde 管「形状」（字段在不在、类型对不对），`ConfigError` 管「语义」（跨字段与内核不变量）；`Option` 字段的存在让「缺失」能被类型化报告而不是与取值混淆。
- `TryFrom<RawConfig> for Config35` 是唯一校验边界：十步有序检查、首错即返；通过之后下游拿到的配置「已知可加载」，无需重复防御。
- `layer_types` 在这里完成从字符串到 `LayerType` 的升格，混合架构（full/linear 两种层的排布）自此成为类型里的一等信息。
- 内核维度（128/128、256、1..=4）是构建期烘焙的 AOT 常量，配置期对拍让「内核不兼容」在加载时就 fail-closed，而不是首次启动时炸 CUDA 错误。
- 三个词表宽度各司其职：`vocab_size`（物理行）→ `decodable_vocab`（稠密可解码前缀，fail-closed 拒绝过宽 tokenizer 与稀疏 id）→ `selection_vocab`（128 对齐、夹紧，喂给 cublasLt 快路径）。
- `Config35` 刻意对张量并行无知——TP 几何留给下一讲的 `LocalGeometry`，那是方向性边界的另一半。

tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
